fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Hailing from Sweden, Joakim Häggström is a musician and a researcher of lost mythology & history. He's also been involved with music, sound and frequency for many years and in this episode we weave between discussions of sonic phenomenon and correspondences, legends from Northern European lands, the Emerald Tablets of Hermes, and much more.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Heathen Roots Beneath Christian Forms", "body": "A symbol on Joakim's mug opens a wider claim: the tongue sticking out across European heraldry, he says, is a heathen emblem of offering and drinking. He describes the Templars and the orders tied to John the Baptist, the Knights of Malta among them, as an underground movement of the old heathen families, founded around the eleventh and twelfth centuries and fading before the French Revolution. Even baptism, in his telling, began as their rite, and he points to an old baptismal cauldron found on Gotland, far older than Christianity there, as a sign that it first honored a life water, the water of wisdom."}, {"title": "Unpacking Words Down to Their Sounds", "body": "Chance splits Ouroboros into our O bore us, the all that carried and birthed us, and notes how many meanings hide in bore. Joakim hears borg in it, a nest or a castle, and the pair tie the sound to Hyperborea, the northern homeland. Freedom gets the same treatment: fri means free in Swedish and English alike, while dom means judgment, and Joakim explains that every letter once carried its own meaning, from A as awesome and B as a castle to D as daylight and E as the oak. Culture, he says, is kul tour, a funny trip, and he believes the old society existed to lift everyone up."}, {"title": "The Tour Friend and the Saga's Long Road", "body": "Joakim describes the tour friend: every three years you paired with a new best friend, toured together on Thursdays, traded skills, and at the end gave them a token such as a handmade necklace. Chance contrasts it with the master and apprentice model, where the only real difference is that one person is older and has learned something. The talk then turns to Ior Bock, who spent twenty years, from age 7 to 27, receiving the saga two hours a day. Joakim says it could only be released in 1984, the close of a 10,000 year heathen cycle, under an agreement dating back to Birger Jarl, the founder of Stockholm."}, {"title": "Gustav Vasa and the Swedish Break With Rome", "body": "Joakim recounts how Christian the Tyrant of Denmark gathered Sweden's leading nobles in Stockholm and killed them in the Stockholm Bloodbath, while Gustav Vasa, whose father died there, arrived late and could only watch from a window. With money borrowed from Lübeck, a small fleet and a rallied army, Vasa retook the country within a few years, expelled the bishop and built a Swedish church that kept taxes out of the Vatican's hands. He melted church bells into cannons, and Joakim links him to the Bock family, whose help he says rebuilt Hel as Helsinki after it had long lain deserted."}, {"title": "Where Souls and Spirits Go", "body": "Chance suggests memory and identity live in the body's electromagnetic field, drawn at death toward the pole the way the Earth reclaims a charge. Joakim separates soul from spirit: the soul lives in the body's cells, while the spirit rides the breath, as the Swedish words ande and andas, spirit and breathing, still show. In the old story all souls go to Valhalla regardless of deeds. The dead were burned and their ashes placed in a family oak, so a person could rise through the tree and become a leaf, and rooting its branches back into the old trunk could keep that tree alive indefinitely."}]
